Company.title: Company
Company.description: Represents an individual company or tenant within the PCGMANTENIMIENTO SaaS platform. All company-specific data is isolated under this entity.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Company entity.

name.description: The official name of the company.

rut.description: The Chilean tax identification number (RUT) for the company.

address.description: The physical address of the company.

contactEmail.description: The primary contact email address for the company.

contactPhone.description: The primary contact phone number for the company.

isActive.description: Indicates if the company's account is currently active and can access the platform, typically linked to subscription status.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the company record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp of the last update to the company record.

User.title: User
User.description: Represents an individual user accessing the PCGMANTENIMIENTO platform, either as a superadmin or with roles within a specific company.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

companyId.description: Reference to the Company this user belongs to. Null for 'superadmin' role. (Relationship: Company 1:N User)

email.description: The user's email address, used for login.

firstName.description: The first name of the user.

lastName.description: The last name of the user.

role.description: The role of the user, defining their permissions within a company or the platform. Possible values: 'superadmin', 'companyAdmin', 'supervisor', 'tecnico', 'reviewer'.

isActive.description: Indicates if the user's account is currently active.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp of the last update to the user record.

WorkOrder.title: WorkOrder
WorkOrder.description: Represents a maintenance work order, tracking its lifecycle and details from creation to approval or rejection.

id.description: Unique identifier for the WorkOrder entity.

companyId.description: Reference to the Company that owns this work order. (Relationship: Company 1:N WorkOrder)

title.description: A concise title or summary for the work order.

description.description: Detailed description of the maintenance task or issue.

status.description: The current status of the work order. Possible values: 'creada', 'asignada', 'ejecutada', 'enRevision', 'aprobada', 'rechazada'.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the work order was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp of the last update to the work order record.

createdByUserId.description: Reference to the User who created this work order. (Relationship: User 1:N WorkOrder)

assignedToUserId.description: Reference to the User (tecnico or supervisor) currently assigned to this work order. (Relationship: User 1:N WorkOrder)

scheduledDateTime.description: Planned date and time for the work order execution.

completedDateTime.description: Actual date and time when the work order was marked as completed.

priority.description: The urgency level of the work order. Possible values: 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'urgent'.

locationDescription.description: A description of the physical location where the maintenance work is to be performed.

reviewerRequired.description: Indicates if a formal review by a 'reviewer' role is mandatory for this specific work order before it can be approved.

DigitalLogbookEntry.title: DigitalLogbookEntry
DigitalLogbookEntry.description: Represents an immutable, auditable entry in the digital logbook associated with a specific Work Order, recording all significant events and changes.

id.description: Unique identifier for the DigitalLogbookEntry entity.

workOrderId.description: Reference to the WorkOrder this logbook entry belongs to. (Relationship: WorkOrder 1:N DigitalLogbookEntry)

companyId.description: Reference to the Company that owns the parent work order. Denormalized for efficient queries and security rules. (Relationship: Company 1:N DigitalLogbookEntry)

timestamp.description: Timestamp when this logbook event occurred.

eventType.description: The type of event recorded in this logbook entry. Possible values: 'statusChange', 'commentAdded', 'fileAttached', 'reviewInitiated', 'reviewCompleted', 'workOrderApproved', 'workOrderRejected', 'workOrderCreated', 'workOrderAssigned', 'workOrderExecuted'.

actorUserId.description: Reference to the User who performed the action recorded by this entry. (Relationship: User 1:N DigitalLogbookEntry)

details.description: A descriptive text providing more context about the event.

oldValue.description: The value of a field before the change (e.g., previous status), if applicable.

newValue.description: The new value of a field after the change (e.g., new status), if applicable.

isImmutable.description: Flag indicating that this logbook entry, once associated with an approved WorkOrder, cannot be modified.

Review.title: Review
Review.description: Represents the formal review process for a WorkOrder, typically performed by an external 'reviewer' role, leading to approval or rejection.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Review entity.

workOrderId.description: Reference to the WorkOrder being reviewed. (Relationship: WorkOrder 1:0..1 Review)

companyId.description: Reference to the Company that owns the work order. Denormalized for efficient queries and security rules. (Relationship: Company 1:N Review)

reviewerId.description: Reference to the User (with 'reviewer' role) who performed this review. (Relationship: User 1:N Review)

status.description: The outcome of the review. Possible values: 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected'.

submittedAt.description: Timestamp when the review was submitted (started).

reviewedAt.description: Timestamp when the review was completed (approved or rejected).

comments.description: Optional comments or feedback provided by the reviewer.

decisionDetails.description: Specific reasons or notes pertaining to the review decision (approval or rejection).

Subscription.title: Subscription
Subscription.description: Manages a company's subscription details to the PCGMANTENIMIENTO SaaS platform, including plan, status, and billing information.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Subscription entity.

companyId.description: Reference to the Company that holds this subscription. (Relationship: Company 1:N Subscription)

planName.description: The name of the subscription plan (e.g., 'Free', 'Basic', 'Premium', 'Enterprise').

startDate.description: The date when the subscription became active.

endDate.description: The date when the subscription is scheduled to expire or renew.

status.description: The current status of the subscription. Possible values: 'active', 'trial', 'cancelled', 'expired', 'pending'.

priceAmount.description: The monetary amount charged for the subscription plan.

priceCurrency.description: The currency code for the subscription price (e.g., 'CLP', 'USD').

paymentFrequency.description: How often the subscription is billed. Possible values: 'monthly', 'annually'.

autoRenew.description: Indicates if the subscription is set to automatically renew at the end of its term.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the subscription record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp of the last update to the subscription record.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure for PCGMANTENIMIENTO is designed with a strong emphasis on multi-tenancy, granular role-based access control (RBAC), and adherence to the core design principles of authorization independence, structural segregation, and predictable data.  

**Multi-Tenancy and Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):**
The cornerstone of this design is the `/companies/{companyId}` root collection. All company-specific data – `users`, `workOrders`, `subscriptions`, and their respective subcollections (`digitalLogbookEntries`, `reviews`) – are nested directly under their parent `/companies/{companyId}` path. This establishes a strict data isolation boundary for each tenant. Critically, to achieve **Authorization Independence**, every document in these subcollections (e.g., `users`, `workOrders`, `subscriptions`, `digitalLogbookEntries`, `reviews`) will explicitly include a `companyId` field, denormalizing the parent's identifier. For `digitalLogbookEntries` and `reviews`, the `workOrderId` will also be denormalized. This eliminates the need for `get()` calls in Firestore security rules to check parent document attributes, which is essential for atomic operations (transactions/batches) and robust rule evaluation. Rules can directly check `request.auth.uid`'s associated `companyId` (from their user document) against the `companyId` field in the document they are trying to access, making permission checks efficient and clear.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters) and Structural Segregation:**
Each collection (e.g., `users`, `workOrders`, `digitalLogbookEntries`) is designed to have a **homogeneous security posture**. For instance, all documents within `/companies/{companyId}/workOrders` share the same fundamental security requirements: they belong to `companyId` and are accessible based on roles within that company. There is no mixing of public/private or draft/published items in the same collection (e.g., no 'public work orders' mixed with 'private work orders'). This structural segregation greatly simplifies security rules.  

For `list` operations (queries), the structure inherently supports QAPs. Because `companyId` is denormalized in every relevant document, a query like `db.collection('companies').doc(myCompanyId).collection('workOrders').where('status', '==', 'aprobada')` can be secured by a rule that simply checks if `request.auth.uid` belongs to `myCompanyId` and has the necessary role. The `companyId` in the path and denormalized in the document ensures the query is naturally scoped, and rules don't need to filter results after the fact.  

**User & Role Management (DBAC):**
Users are split into two logical groups based on their role: platform `superadmins` and company-specific users. `superadmins` reside in a root collection `/superAdmins/{userId}`, employing the **Existence over Content** pattern for global roles. Company-specific users are in `/companies/{companyId}/users/{userId}`, where their `role` (`companyAdmin`, `supervisor`, `tecnico`, `reviewer`) and `companyId` are explicitly stored. This makes user authentication and role-based authorization in security rules straightforward and highly auditable, relying solely on `request.auth.uid` and database-stored roles.

**Work Order Flow & Digital Logbook:**
The `WorkOrder` entity includes a `status` field (Finite State Machine: `creada` → `asignada` → `ejecutada` → `enRevision` → `aprobada`/`rechazada`) and a `reviewerRequired` boolean flag to manage the optional reviewer workflow. The `DigitalLogbookEntry` subcollection ensures an immutable, auditable record of all work order events. Its `isImmutable` field, enforced by security rules, guarantees the integrity of the audit trail once a work order is approved.

**Scalability and Security Justification:**
*   **Scalability:** The `/companies/{companyId}` root collection inherently shards data by tenant, preventing read/write hot spots across companies. Denormalization reduces cross-document reads, improving performance. The design avoids overly deep or complex hierarchies, which are often performance bottlenecks.
*   **Security:** Path-based authorization (`/companies/{companyId}/...`) combined with denormalized `companyId` fields provides a highly secure multi-tenant environment. Role information stored directly in user documents (or the `superAdmins` collection) enables fine-grained RBAC with simple security rules. The `isImmutable` flag for logbook entries offers strong data integrity. The explicit `reviewerRequired` field in `WorkOrder` allows flexible workflow configuration directly within the data model, without compromising security rules.

This architecture provides a robust, efficient, and easily auditable foundation for the PCGMANTENIMIENTO ERP SaaS platform.
